title: Meccan and Medinan
hookLine: early Meccan surahs are short, poetic, about the One and the Day, the later Medinan ones longer and communal

lines: THE BACK AND THE FRONT OF THE BOOK.
cards: There's the way you talk when you're trying to wake someone up, and the way you talk when you're helping them set up a new home. The first is short, urgent, vivid: look, listen, get up.

The second is longer and practical: here's how we'll share the kitchen, here's what's fair, here's who pays for what. Open the Qur'an near the back, then near the front, and you'll hear something like that difference.

teach.b: The Prophet's mission had two halves: about thirteen years in Mecca, where the Muslims were a small and often persecuted group; then the hijra, the move to Medina, and about ten years building a community.

Scholars sort the surahs by these two periods, and printed copies often say at the top of each surah whether it's Makki or Madani, Meccan or Medinan. Scholars differ on where a handful of surahs belong.

teach.h: MECCAN: SHORT, THE ONE AND THE DAY
teach.b: The Meccan surahs, mostly toward the back, tend to be short, with a rhythm and rhyme that ring. They speak of the One God, the Day of Judgment, the signs in nature, the prophets who came before.
Many open with oaths: by the dawn, by the fig, by time. Take Surah 112: "Say: He is Allah, the One!" Four lines, and it's done.

The Medinan surahs, mostly toward the front, tend to be long. They speak to a community: prayer, fasting and charity, marriage and inheritance, contracts, war and peace, how to live beside neighbors of other faiths.
Al-Baqarah is Medinan; its verses on fasting in Ramadan come from Medina.
A detail scholars care about: the definition al-Suyuti calls the best known goes by time, not place, before the hijra or after it.
So a verse revealed in Mecca years after the hijra, during the farewell pilgrimage, still counts as Medinan. And some surahs hold verses from both periods.
Muslims speak of one book here, not two: one voice speaking to one people at two stages of their life. First the heart woken, then the house put in order.

how: Printed copies of the Qur'an usually mark each surah as Meccan or Medinan, and Muslims studying a verse learn which period it comes from to understand what it was answering.

games.q: during the farewell pilgrimage, years after the hijra, a verse is revealed in Mecca itself. how does the best-known definition label it?
o: Medinan, because it came after the hijra.
games.why: the best-known definition sorts by time, not place. anything after the hijra is Medinan, even when it came in Mecca.

practice: Open a mushaf or an app to al-Ikhlas and read its four lines, then turn to any page near the start of al-Baqarah and simply look at it, without reading it all: a bell's ring, and a long conversation.
If you can't open them now, say al-Ikhlas from memory and picture a full page of close lines beside it, then rest in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Hijra. The Prophet's move to Medina — the line by which scholars sort every surah as Meccan or Medinan, before it or after. Today's word.
